principles.general: Solid move. Keep developing and fighting for the center.
principles.centerPawn: Good: {{piece}} move helps control the center.
principles.development: Development: {{piece}} gets into play and supports the center.
principles.castle: Good: castling improves king safety and connects the rooks.
principles.earlyQueen: Careful: early queen moves can be risky. Prioritize development.
principles.kingSafety: Consider castling soon to improve king safety.
principles.enPassant: Nice! En passant is a rare tactical capture.

tips.title: Why this move?
tips.check: Checks are forcing—your opponent must respond.
tips.knightRim: Knights on the rim are dim—consider central squares.
tips.fianchetto: This prepares a fianchetto, strengthening the long diagonal.
tips.wingPawn: Early wing pawn moves can be committal—watch your center.
tips.kingMove: Moving the king early can be risky; look for safer squares.

italian.name: Italian Game
italian.note: A classical opening focused on rapid development and central control.
italian.history: Documented in the 16th century; analyzed by Greco in the 1620s.

ruyLopez.name: Ruy Lopez
ruyLopez.note: A strategic opening that pressures the center and targets the knight on c6.
ruyLopez.history: Named after Ruy López de Segura (1561).

sicilian.name: Sicilian Defense
sicilian.note: Asymmetric structure that fights for the center from the flank.
sicilian.history: First recorded in the late 16th century; mainline in the 20th.

french.name: French Defense
french.note: Solid structure aiming for counterplay against White's center.

caroKann.name: Caro-Kann Defense
caroKann.note: Resilient defense aiming for a strong pawn structure.
caroKann.history: Introduced by Caro and Kann in 1886.

scandinavian.name: Scandinavian Defense
scandinavian.history: Known since the 19th century; revived in modern play.

petrov.name: Petrov Defense
petrov.note: Solid and symmetrical, aiming for equal play.
petrov.history: Introduced by Alexander Petrov in the 1820s.

philidor.name: Philidor Defense
philidor.note: A compact defense that supports a later central break.

queensGambit.name: Queen's Gambit
queensGambit.note: White offers a pawn to gain space and central control.
queensGambit.history: Analyzed since the 15th century; key line of classical chess.

queensGambitDeclined.name: Queen's Gambit Declined
queensGambitDeclined.note: Black holds the center and aims for solid development.
queensGambitDeclined.history: Solid mainline since the early 20th century.

kingsIndian.name: King's Indian Defense
kingsIndian.note: Black allows space but prepares a dynamic counterattack.
kingsIndian.history: Developed in the 1950s as a dynamic defense.

english.name: English Opening
english.note: Flexible opening that builds control of the center from the side.

italianTwoKnights.name: Italian Game: Two Knights
italianTwoKnights.note: Sharp development with early pressure on f7.
italianTwoKnights.history: Popular in 19th-century romantic chess for its tactics.

italianGiuocoPiano.name: Giuoco Piano
italianGiuocoPiano.note: A quiet Italian line with flexible maneuvering.
italianGiuocoPiano.history: Studied since the 18th century for strategic plans.

italianEvansGambit.name: Evans Gambit
italianEvansGambit.note: White gambits a pawn for rapid development and attack.
italianEvansGambit.history: Popularized by W. D. Evans in the 1820s; used by Morphy.

ruyLopezBerlin.name: Ruy Lopez: Berlin Defense
ruyLopezBerlin.note: Solid defense aiming for a durable endgame.
ruyLopezBerlin.history: Revived at elite level by Kramnik in 2000.

ruyLopezExchange.name: Ruy Lopez: Exchange
ruyLopezExchange.note: Early simplification that damages Black’s pawn structure.

scotch.name: Scotch Game
scotch.note: Open central play and rapid piece activity.
scotch.history: Popularized in the 1820s; still a mainline choice.

vienna.name: Vienna Game
vienna.note: Flexible development with an early Nc3.
vienna.history: Popular in Vienna clubs in the 1820s–1840s.

kingsGambit.name: King's Gambit
kingsGambit.note: Aggressive pawn gambit for rapid development and attack.
kingsGambit.history: Known since the 17th century; a staple of 19th-century romantic chess.

sicilianNajdorf.name: Sicilian Najdorf
sicilianNajdorf.note: Dynamic and complex, rich with tactical ideas.
sicilianNajdorf.history: Developed in the 20th century; a favorite of Kasparov.

queensIndian.name: Queen's Indian Defense
queensIndian.history: Developed in the 1920s; used by Nimzowitsch.

benoni.name: Modern Benoni Defense
benoni.history: Revived in the 1930s; became mainline in the 1950s.

benkoGambit.name: Benko Gambit
benkoGambit.note: Pawn sacrifice for long-term queenside pressure.
benkoGambit.history: Introduced by Pal Benko in the 1960s.

london.name: London System
london.note: Simple setup with strong central control.
london.history: Popular in modern play for its practical plans.

nimzoIndian.name: Nimzo-Indian Defense
nimzoIndian.note: Black pressures White’s center and structure.

grunfeld.name: Grünfeld Defense
grunfeld.note: Black attacks the center with piece activity.
grunfeld.history: Named after Ernst Grünfeld, popular since the 1920s.

sicilianClassical.name: Sicilian Classical
sicilianClassical.history: A mainline since the early 20th century.

sicilianDragon.name: Sicilian Dragon
sicilianDragon.note: Sharp line with a fianchetto and opposite-side attacks.
sicilianDragon.history: Popularized in the mid-20th century for its tactics.

sicilianAcceleratedDragon.name: Sicilian Accelerated Dragon
sicilianAcceleratedDragon.note: Fast fianchetto without ...d6, aiming for activity.

frenchAdvance.name: French Advance
frenchAdvance.note: White gains space and restricts Black’s pieces.

frenchTarrasch.name: French Tarrasch
frenchTarrasch.note: Solid structure with clear plans for development.
frenchTarrasch.history: Associated with Tarrasch in the late 19th century.

caroKannClassical.name: Caro-Kann Classical
caroKannClassical.note: A sturdy line with clear development for both sides.
caroKannClassical.history: Standard line since the early 20th century.

alekhine.name: Alekhine Defense
alekhine.note: Provokes the center and aims to undermine it.
alekhine.history: Introduced by Alexander Alekhine in the 1920s.

queensGambitAccepted.name: Queen's Gambit Accepted
queensGambitAccepted.note: Black takes the pawn and aims for active piece play.
queensGambitAccepted.history: Played since the 19th century at high level.

queensGambitOrthodox.name: QGD Orthodox
queensGambitOrthodox.note: Classical development with solid central structure.
queensGambitOrthodox.history: A major mainline from the early 20th century.

kingsIndianMainline.name: King's Indian Main Line
kingsIndianMainline.note: Both sides build strong centers before attacking.
kingsIndianMainline.history: Developed in the 1950s and popular in modern play.

pirc.name: Pirc Defense
pirc.note: Flexible setup inviting White to build a big center.
pirc.history: Named after Vasja Pirc; popular in mid-20th century.
